newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica to get laws improving investor protection.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica to get laws improving investor protection.

text.p: South Africa's parliamentary finance committee on Tuesday approved the first of about 20 bills intended to improve investor protection.

The Financial Services Board, which regulates and supervises the financial services industry, excluding banks, proposed the bills to increase its powers to act against dishonesty or fraud committed by financial brokers.
The board's head of Research, Franso van Zyl, said the Financial Institutions Amendment Bill contained the most urgent of a wide range of legal amendments.
It would now go to parliament for approval by the legislature.
Van Zyl said that two other bills approved by the cabinet were being finalised for the short- and long-term insurance industries.
The board, a statutory body, oversees the insurance industry, unit trusts, participation bonds, pension funds, the stock exchange and the money market.
